boss.q: A student says elasticity is just the direction of a change. What correction is needed?
options: Elasticity measures the size of a percentage response relative to a percentage change
Elasticity records only whether demand slopes down
Elasticity is the market price divided by income
Elasticity is another name for total revenue
boss.feedback: Elasticity adds magnitude to direction by comparing percentage changes.

boss.q: Which coefficient represents the strongest demand response to price?
boss.feedback: The larger absolute coefficient indicates greater responsiveness.

boss.q: Which observation is consistent with inelastic demand?
options: Price rises 5 percent and quantity demanded falls 15 percent
Price falls 8 percent and quantity demanded rises 16 percent
Price rises 10 percent and quantity demanded falls 4 percent
Any change where quantity moves opposite price
boss.feedback: A smaller proportional quantity response than price change means inelastic demand.

boss.q: Which change most likely makes brand-level demand more elastic?
options: Consumers become locked into annual contracts
The purchase becomes more necessary
Buyers have less time to adjust
Several close competing brands enter
boss.feedback: More close substitutes increase switching.

boss.q: Which product characteristic most likely reduces demand elasticity?
options: The item is a necessity with few substitutes
The item is a luxury with many substitutes
The market is narrowly defined
The purchase takes a large budget share
boss.feedback: Necessity and few substitutes limit response.

boss.q: Why is demand for one brand of salt more elastic than demand for salt as a category?
options: Salt is measured in pounds
The brand has many close substitutes within the category
Category demand has a flatter slope in every graph
Brand demand ignores consumer preferences
boss.feedback: Narrower markets have more alternatives.

boss.q: A vertical demand curve has elasticity:
options: One
Infinity
Zero
A value that rises with price
boss.feedback: Quantity is fixed as price changes.

boss.q: A horizontal demand curve has elasticity:
options: Zero
One
Negative one
Effectively infinite
boss.feedback: An arbitrarily small price increase causes demand to vanish.

boss.q: A seller raises price and total revenue falls. What does the total-revenue test imply?
options: Demand is elastic
Demand is inelastic
Demand is perfectly inelastic
Supply is elastic
boss.feedback: Revenue moving opposite price indicates elastic demand.

boss.q: A seller raises price and total revenue rises. What does the total-revenue test imply?
options: Demand is elastic
Demand is inelastic
Demand is unit elastic
Income elasticity is positive
boss.feedback: Revenue moving with price indicates inelastic demand.

boss.q: Which statement about unit-elastic demand is correct?
options: Quantity does not respond to price
A price increase always raises revenue
The percentage changes offset, leaving total revenue about unchanged
Demand is horizontal
boss.feedback: Unit elasticity leaves revenue approximately unchanged for small changes.

boss.q: Which situation most likely has highly inelastic short-run supply?
options: Mass-produced notebooks next year
Cloud storage with unused servers
A storable manufactured input
Tickets for a stadium event already underway
boss.feedback: Event capacity cannot be expanded after the event begins.

boss.q: Supply becomes more elastic over time mainly because producers can:
options: Change capacity, enter, exit, and substitute inputs
Make demand shift automatically
Eliminate scarcity
Set any price without losing buyers
boss.feedback: Longer horizons expand production adjustments.

boss.q: A positive income elasticity identifies:
options: An inferior good
A normal good
Complements
Perfectly inelastic demand
boss.feedback: Demand for a normal good moves with income.

boss.q: A negative income elasticity identifies:
options: A normal good
Substitutes
An inferior good
Elastic supply
boss.feedback: Demand for an inferior good moves opposite income.

boss.q: A positive cross-price elasticity identifies:
options: Complements
Inferior goods
Perfectly elastic goods
Substitutes
boss.feedback: Demand for one rises with the other’s price when goods substitute.

boss.q: A negative cross-price elasticity identifies:
options: Complements
Substitutes
Normal goods
Unrelated goods by definition
boss.feedback: Demand for one falls when the other’s price rises.

boss.q: Which side of a market bears more of a tax, other things equal?
options: The side named in the law
The side with lower elasticity
The side with the flatter curve regardless of axes
The side with more participants
boss.feedback: The less responsive side has fewer avoidance options.

boss.q: Checkpoint: At point B, what does the graph imply about total revenue for a small movement in either direction along the same linear demand curve?
options: Total revenue is locally maximized.
Total revenue rises for small movements in both directions.
Total revenue is unchanged at every lower price.
Total revenue is zero at the midpoint.
boss.feedback: At B the linear demand curve is unit elastic and revenue is at its local maximum. A small movement in either direction lowers revenue; the first-order change is zero at the exact maximum.

boss.q: Checkpoint: Which displayed demand curve has zero price elasticity?
options: D2
D1
Both D1 and D2
Neither D1 nor D2
boss.feedback: D2 is vertical, so quantity does not respond to price and elasticity is zero.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for music subscriptions when price rises from $10 to $12 and quantity demanded falls from 1,000 to 800?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 1.22.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for farmers-market baskets when price falls from $30 to $27 and quantity demanded rises from 500 to 620?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 2.04.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for parking permits when price rises from $60 to $72 and quantity demanded falls from 2,000 to 1,700?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 0.89.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for fitness classes when price rises from $20 to $24 and quantity demanded falls from 1,500 to 1,200?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 1.22.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for intercity tickets when price falls from $50 to $45 and quantity demanded rises from 800 to 960?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 1.73.

boss.q: Using the midpoint method, what is the price elasticity of demand for cloud-service plans when price rises from $100 to $115 and quantity demanded falls from 900 to 720?
boss.feedback: The midpoint coefficient is approximately 1.59.

boss.q: A price cut raises quantity 18 percent while price falls 9 percent. What happens to total revenue?
options: It rises because demand is elastic
It falls because demand is inelastic
It remains unchanged because both variables changed
It cannot be determined without income
boss.feedback: Elasticity is 2, so quantity rises proportionally more than price falls.

boss.q: A price increase of 12 percent reduces quantity by 3 percent. Which conclusion follows?
options: Demand is elastic, so total revenue falls
Demand is inelastic, so total revenue likely rises
Demand is unit elastic
Demand is perfectly elastic
boss.feedback: Elasticity is 0.25; the price effect dominates revenue.

boss.q: At the midpoint of a linear demand curve, which pair is correct?
options: Perfect inelasticity and zero revenue
Elastic demand and negative marginal revenue
Unit elasticity and maximum total revenue
Inelastic demand and positive marginal revenue
boss.feedback: The midpoint of a linear demand curve is unit elastic and revenue-maximizing.

boss.q: A firm operates on the inelastic portion of demand with positive marginal cost. Why is that inconsistent with profit maximization?
options: A price cut would necessarily raise profit
Marginal revenue is positive there
Demand must be horizontal
A price increase would raise revenue while reducing output cost
boss.feedback: Inelastic demand implies negative marginal revenue.

boss.q: A 5 percent income increase raises demand 7.5 percent. What is income elasticity?
The price of tea rises 10 percent and demand for coffee rises 6 percent. What is cross-price elasticity?
boss.feedback: 6 ÷ 10 = 0.6, indicating substitutes.

boss.q: The price of printers rises 8 percent and demand for ink falls 12 percent. What is cross-price elasticity?
boss.feedback: −12 ÷ 8 = −1.5, indicating complements.

boss.q: The price of greenhouse vegetables rises 20 percent and output rises 10 percent. Supply is:
options: Elastic with elasticity 2
Unit elastic
Perfectly inelastic
Inelastic with elasticity 0.5

boss.q: Which market is likely to have the greatest tax-created quantity reduction?
options: One with elastic demand and elastic supply
One with inelastic demand and inelastic supply
One where sellers remit the tax
One with a negative income elasticity
boss.feedback: Responsive buyers and sellers reduce transactions more strongly.

boss.q: Demand is elastic and supply is inelastic. Who bears more of a tax?
options: Buyers
Sellers
The statutory payer
The burden must split equally
boss.feedback: Sellers are the less elastic side.

boss.q: A hotel can separate business and leisure guests. Business demand is less elastic. Which rate pattern fits elasticity-based pricing?
options: Lower business rates and higher leisure rates
Identical rates regardless of resale
Higher business rates and lower leisure rates
Zero leisure rates
boss.feedback: The less elastic group can sustain a higher price.

boss.q: A gasoline tax generates relatively stable revenue but barely changes consumption. What does that suggest?
options: Demand is highly elastic
Supply is perfectly elastic by definition
Cross-price elasticity is negative
Demand is inelastic over the observed range
boss.feedback: A small quantity response and stable base indicate inelastic demand.

boss.q: Refer to the graph. Checkpoint: Calculate total revenue at C, B, and A. Which pattern is correct as price falls across those points?
options: Revenue falls through every interval because price falls at each point
Revenue rises in the elastic region, peaks at unit elasticity, then falls in the inelastic region
Revenue stays constant through every interval because the curve has constant slope over the shown interval
Revenue peaks in the inelastic region, then rises as demand becomes more elastic
boss.feedback: The total-revenue test tracks the shift from elastic demand above the midpoint to unit elasticity at B and inelastic demand below it.

boss.q: Checkpoint: The two supply curves share the same starting point and face the same price increase. Which graph-based reason makes the long-run curve more elastic?
options: Its quantity response is larger
Its price change is larger
Its starting quantity is smaller
Its curve is vertical
boss.feedback: With the same price change and starting point, the long-run curve shows the larger percentage quantity response.

boss.q: A tax is imposed with perfectly inelastic demand. The law is changed so buyers remit it instead of sellers. What changes?
options: Only remittance changes; buyers still bear the burden
Sellers now bear the full burden
The burden becomes equal
The tax no longer affects price
boss.feedback: Perfectly inelastic buyers cannot avoid the tax; statutory incidence is irrelevant.

boss.q: A permanent tax initially falls heavily on producers, but supply becomes more elastic over time. What is likely?
options: All burden shifts toward producers
More long-run burden shifts toward buyers
Burden cannot change over time
The tax becomes a subsidy
boss.feedback: As producers gain exit options, demand becomes relatively less elastic.

boss.q: A binding rent ceiling persists for years. Housing supply becomes more elastic over time. What happens to the shortage?
options: It disappears because supply is elastic
It remains identical
It grows as quantity supplied responds more to the below-market rent
Quantity demanded falls because rent is lower
boss.feedback: Long-run supply contraction magnifies the shortage.

boss.q: A farm quota reduces output. Under what demand condition can farm revenue rise?
options: Elastic demand
Perfectly elastic demand
Positive cross-price elasticity alone
Inelastic demand
boss.feedback: With inelastic demand, the price rise dominates the quantity loss.

boss.q: A monopolist’s demand elasticity at the current output is 0.8. What does this reveal?
options: Demand is inelastic with negative marginal revenue
The firm is at maximum profit
Marginal revenue is positive
Demand is perfectly elastic
boss.feedback: A profit-maximizing monopolist with positive marginal cost does not operate on inelastic demand.

boss.q: Demand is Q = 120 − 3P. At P = 30, Q = 30. What is point elasticity?
Supply is Q = 20 + 2P. At P = 20, Q = 60. What is point elasticity?
options: About 0.67

boss.q: A 10 percent price increase lowers quantity 20 percent. Cost per unit is unchanged. Which revenue-profit statement is safest?
options: Both revenue and profit must rise
Profit must fall by exactly 10 percent
Revenue is unchanged
Revenue falls, but profit direction still requires cost information
boss.feedback: Elasticity determines revenue direction, but profit also depends on costs.

boss.q: A rival price cut reduces a firm’s demand 15 percent. The rival price fell 10 percent. What is cross-price elasticity?
options: 1.5, indicating substitutes
−1.5, indicating complements
0.67, indicating substitutes
The relationship cannot be measured

boss.q: Income falls 4 percent and demand for a product rises 6 percent. What is income elasticity and classification?
options: 1.5; normal good
−1.5; inferior good
−0.67; complement
0.67; normal good

boss.q: A tariff is placed on imports with highly elastic import demand. What is most likely?
options: Import quantity barely changes
Foreign supply becomes perfectly inelastic automatically
Import quantity falls sharply and tariff revenue may be fragile
Consumers bear no burden
boss.feedback: Elastic import demand responds strongly to the tariff-inclusive price.

boss.q: A minimum wage raises employment costs by 10 percent in a market where the elasticity of labor demand is 1.4. What is the approximate percentage change in employment?
options: A 7.1 percent decline
A 14 percent increase
No effect because wages are not output prices
A 14 percent decline
boss.feedback: 1.4 × 10% = 14% in the opposite direction.

boss.q: A city’s congestion toll goal is quantity reduction, not revenue. Which companion policy improves effectiveness?
options: Expand close transit substitutes
Reduce transit availability
Shorten advance notice
Make parking cheaper downtown
boss.feedback: Better substitutes make trip demand more elastic.

boss.q: A product is a necessity but one brand has many rivals. Which elasticity comparison is correct?
options: Both must be inelastic
Brand demand can be elastic while category demand remains inelastic
Category demand must be more elastic
Necessity eliminates market-definition effects
boss.feedback: The relevant substitute set differs by market definition.

boss.q: A regression slope is −200 units per dollar. Why is this not enough to classify elasticity?
options: Negative slopes are always elastic
All slopes below −1 are elastic
Elasticity also requires the current price and quantity scale
Elasticity uses only units per dollar
boss.feedback: Point elasticity scales the slope by P/Q.

boss.q: A market has relatively inelastic demand and supply. If the good is taxed, which combination is most likely?
options: Unstable revenue and large quantity distortion
No tax burden
Perfectly equal incidence
Relatively stable revenue and comparatively small quantity distortion
boss.feedback: Low responsiveness preserves transactions and the tax base.

boss.q: A firm estimates the price elasticity of demand to be 2 near its current price. Why should it not assume the same responsiveness after a 50 percent price cut?
options: Elasticity can vary along the curve and outside the estimated range
Elasticity cannot be used for price cuts
Demand becomes vertical after large changes
Only income elasticity varies
boss.feedback: Local estimates may not extrapolate to large changes.

boss.q: A seller segments customers by elasticity, but low-price customers can resell. What is the main problem?
options: Demand becomes perfectly inelastic
Arbitrage collapses the price separation
Marginal cost becomes negative
Income elasticity becomes zero
boss.feedback: Resale undermines third-degree price discrimination.

boss.q: Checkpoint: Using the two labeled points on vertical D2, what is the midpoint price elasticity of demand?
options: Undefined because price changes
boss.feedback: Quantity is unchanged between the two points, so the percentage change in quantity is zero and PED equals zero.

boss.q: Checkpoint: Using the midpoint formula and the displayed short-run and long-run endpoints, which approximate pair correctly compares supply elasticity?
options: Short run 0.75; long run 0.23
Short run 1.00; long run 1.00
Short run 3.25; long run 0.75
Short run 0.23; long run 0.75
boss.feedback: The short-run response is about 0.23 and the long-run response about 0.75, so long-run supply is more elastic.

legendaryBoss.q: A market’s demand becomes more elastic after information improves. What mechanism is most plausible?
options: Sellers lose all production capacity
Income elasticity becomes zero
Buyers can compare prices and substitutes more easily
The statutory tax payer changes
legendaryBoss.feedback: Information lowers search costs and supports substitution.

legendaryBoss.q: A health insurer lowers patients’ out-of-pocket price. What happens to the observed price sensitivity of patients at the point of service?
options: It must become perfectly elastic
It equals provider supply elasticity
It turns into income elasticity
It may look lower because patients pay only part of the price
legendaryBoss.feedback: Insurance reduces the price signal patients directly confront.

legendaryBoss.q: A product’s demand is inelastic at current prices, but a close substitute is scheduled to launch. How should a long-term revenue forecast account for the substitute’s entry?
options: Let elasticity rise after substitute entry
Assume elasticity remains fixed forever
Set elasticity to zero after entry
Use supply elasticity as demand elasticity
legendaryBoss.feedback: Market structure changes can alter responsiveness.

legendaryBoss.q: A policymaker claims a tax on an inelastic good is painless because quantity barely changes. What is missing?
options: Inelastic demand prevents any price change
Burden can be large even when deadweight loss is modest
Tax revenue must be zero
Only elastic goods create burden
legendaryBoss.feedback: Low quantity distortion does not mean no distributional burden.

legendaryBoss.q: A product has very elastic demand and very inelastic supply. A demand increase occurs. Which short-run outcome is most likely?
options: A large quantity increase and tiny price change because demand is elastic
No price change
A relatively large price increase but modest quantity increase because supply constrains expansion
A quantity decrease
legendaryBoss.feedback: For a demand shift, supply elasticity governs how much output can expand; inelastic supply yields a large price response.

legendaryBoss.q: A supply increase occurs in a market with highly elastic demand. Compared with inelastic demand, what happens?
options: Quantity rises less and price falls more
Price and quantity do not change
Total revenue must always rise
Quantity rises more and price falls less
legendaryBoss.feedback: Elastic buyers absorb added supply with a larger quantity response and smaller price decline.

legendaryBoss.q: Why can elasticity estimates differ across demographic groups even for the same product and price?
options: Substitutes, budget shares, preferences, and constraints differ across groups
Elasticity is a physical constant of the product
Different groups use different currencies
Only supply can vary across groups
legendaryBoss.feedback: Elasticity reflects choice context, not just product identity.

legendaryBoss.q: A seller sees no quantity response after a tiny price test. Why is concluding perfectly inelastic demand premature?
options: Any zero observed change proves perfect inelasticity
Noise, contracts, and a tiny test may hide the response
Demand can respond only after a supply shift
Perfect inelasticity is the default
legendaryBoss.feedback: Observed response may be imprecise or constrained over the test window.

legendaryBoss.q: An elasticity estimate is based on a period when income and competitor prices also changed. What is the core identification problem?
options: Elasticity requires no quantity data
The midpoint method cannot use time-series data
The observed quantity change may not be caused solely by the product’s price
Demand must be perfectly elastic
legendaryBoss.feedback: Other demand shifters confound the price-response estimate.

legendaryBoss.q: A firm’s price and quantity move in the same direction after a demand shift. Why can the observed ratio not be treated as price elasticity of demand?
options: Demand elasticity is positive only after shifts
Price elasticity requires supply to be vertical
Same-direction movement proves an inferior good
The movement reflects a shift of demand, not movement along a stable demand curve
legendaryBoss.feedback: Elasticity of demand requires isolating a price change along a given demand relationship.

legendaryBoss.q: A supply shift causes price and quantity to move in opposite directions. Under what condition can the resulting arc approximate demand elasticity?
options: Stable demand plus an exogenous supply shift
Demand also shifts at the same time
The legal tax payer is known
Income elasticity equals one
legendaryBoss.feedback: An exogenous supply shift can trace movement along demand if demand itself is stable.

legendaryBoss.q: A demand shift causes price and quantity supplied to move in the same direction. Under what condition can the resulting arc approximate supply elasticity?
options: Supply also shifts simultaneously
Stable supply plus an exogenous demand shift
Demand is perfectly inelastic
The product is a normal good
legendaryBoss.feedback: An exogenous demand shift can trace movement along a stable supply curve.

legendaryBoss.q: A government publishes one national elasticity for housing. Why should local planners be cautious?
options: Elasticity is never useful for housing
National estimates are always perfectly elastic
Local land, regulation, vacancy, and time horizons differ
Only income elasticity matters locally
legendaryBoss.feedback: Housing responsiveness is highly context-dependent.

legendaryBoss.q: An emergency suddenly makes a product necessary, while production capacity is fixed. What happens to short-run demand and supply responsiveness?
options: Both become perfectly elastic
Demand becomes elastic while supply becomes infinite
Elasticity is unchanged because curves do not shift
Both may become more inelastic, amplifying the price response to a shock
legendaryBoss.feedback: Urgency limits buyer substitution and fixed capacity limits seller response.

legendaryBoss.q: A market has perfectly elastic demand at the world price and upward-sloping domestic supply. A domestic production tax is imposed. What is the likely seller response?
options: Domestic output falls while the consumer price remains pinned near the world price
The consumer price rises by the full tax
Quantity demanded falls along a vertical demand curve
Domestic output is unchanged
legendaryBoss.feedback: With perfectly elastic demand, sellers cannot raise price and must absorb the wedge through net price/output.

legendaryBoss.q: A market has perfectly elastic supply at a given price and downward-sloping demand. A consumption subsidy is offered. What is the likely outcome?
options: Sellers capture the entire benefit through a higher gross price
Buyers receive the benefit through a lower net price and quantity expands
Quantity remains fixed
The subsidy creates no incidence
legendaryBoss.feedback: Perfectly elastic supply keeps the seller price fixed while buyers’ net price falls.

legendaryBoss.q: A seller wants to maximize revenue with one uniform price. What information about elasticity is needed beyond knowing its value at the current price?
options: Only whether the product is normal
Only supply elasticity
Elasticity at the current point and along the curve
The statutory tax rate
legendaryBoss.feedback: Revenue is maximized where elasticity reaches one, requiring location-specific information.

legendaryBoss.q: A firm estimates the price elasticity of demand at 1.05, with a wide confidence interval spanning values below and above one. What is the prudent pricing conclusion?
options: Demand is definitively elastic
Demand is definitively inelastic
Price should be doubled immediately
The revenue effect is uncertain and calls for cautious testing
legendaryBoss.feedback: Sampling uncertainty around one makes the revenue prediction ambiguous.

legendaryBoss.q: A product is a necessity but has many close generic substitutes. Which determinant should dominate brand-level demand?
options: Brand demand can be elastic even when category demand is inelastic
Necessity guarantees every brand is inelastic
Brand and category elasticity must be identical
Supply elasticity determines brand demand
legendaryBoss.feedback: Elasticity depends on the defined choice set.

legendaryBoss.q: A product has no close substitutes today but represents a large budget share. What is the best conclusion?
options: Demand must be perfectly inelastic
The opposing determinants make direct estimation necessary
Demand must be perfectly elastic
Budget share never matters without substitutes
legendaryBoss.feedback: Elasticity determinants are tendencies, not mechanical rules.

legendaryBoss.q: A policymaker compares a steep supply curve and a flat demand curve drawn with different axis scales. What is the proper incidence method?
options: Assign burden to the visually steeper curve
Assign burden to sellers by statute
Compare elasticity estimates, not visual steepness alone
Assume equal burden
legendaryBoss.feedback: Relative percentage responsiveness determines incidence.

legendaryBoss.q: A market’s supply is inelastic today but highly elastic over five years. A permanent tax is imposed. How should incidence analysis change over time?
options: Burden can never change after enactment
Long-run burden shifts entirely to sellers
Tax incidence depends only on the first-year statute
Long-run burden may shift toward the demand side as supply becomes more elastic
legendaryBoss.feedback: Relative elasticities evolve as producers gain exit and adjustment options.

legendaryBoss.q: A temporary tax expires before firms can adjust capacity. Compared with a permanent tax, who may bear more of the temporary tax?
options: Producers, because short-run supply is less elastic
Consumers, because temporary taxes make demand vertical
The government
No one because the tax is temporary
legendaryBoss.feedback: Limited short-run producer adjustment makes supply relatively inelastic.

legendaryBoss.q: A farm-support program wants to raise producer revenue by restricting output. When is the policy most likely to raise total farm revenue?
options: When demand is highly elastic
When demand for the crop is inelastic
When supply is perfectly elastic
When income elasticity is negative
legendaryBoss.feedback: With inelastic demand, the price rise from lower output can outweigh the quantity reduction.

legendaryBoss.q: A seller estimates elastic demand but still raises price after a cost increase. Why is this not necessarily irrational?
options: Elastic demand means price can never rise
Elasticity guarantees profit falls with price
Profit also depends on margin and cost, so a higher price can still be optimal
Costs shift demand rather than supply
legendaryBoss.feedback: Revenue and profit are different objectives; cost pass-through depends on the full optimization problem.

legendaryBoss.q: A firm offers a lower price to customers with more elastic demand. Which condition is essential for the strategy to increase profit?
options: The elastic group must have higher willingness to pay
Both groups must face identical prices
Marginal cost must be zero
The firm must limit resale or switching between customer groups
legendaryBoss.feedback: Segmentation fails if buyers can arbitrage the price difference.

legendaryBoss.q: A country’s demand for foreign currency is derived from import demand. If import demand becomes more elastic, foreign-currency demand is likely to:
options: Become more elastic
Become perfectly inelastic
Become unrelated to import prices
Turn negative at all exchange rates
legendaryBoss.feedback: More responsive import purchases make currency demand more responsive to its effective price.

legendaryBoss.q: A retailer wants to forecast how a rival’s price promotion affects its own sales. Which elasticity is directly relevant?
options: Price elasticity of supply
Cross-price elasticity of demand
Income elasticity only
The rival’s total-revenue elasticity
legendaryBoss.feedback: Cross-price elasticity measures demand response to another product’s price.

legendaryBoss.q: A government forecasts how income growth changes demand for public transit. Which elasticity is directly relevant?
options: Cross-price elasticity
Price elasticity of supply
Income elasticity of demand
Tax incidence elasticity
legendaryBoss.feedback: Income elasticity links demand to income changes.

legendaryBoss.q: A firm wants to predict how much quantity supplied will change when the price it receives for its product changes. Which elasticity is directly relevant?
options: Income elasticity of demand
Cross-price elasticity
Demand elasticity for a complement
Price elasticity of supply
legendaryBoss.feedback: Supply elasticity measures producer quantity response to the output price.

legendaryBoss.q: A researcher reports price elasticity of demand as −2.3 and another reports 2.3 for the same estimate. Are they necessarily inconsistent?
options: No; one reports the signed estimate and one its absolute value
Yes; elasticity can never be negative in any form
Yes; the positive value must be supply elasticity
No; the sign identifies an inferior good
legendaryBoss.feedback: Demand estimates are negative by the law of demand, but classifications commonly use absolute magnitude.

legendaryBoss.q: A researcher reports income elasticity of −2.3. Should the sign be discarded as with price elasticity of demand?
options: Yes; all elasticity signs are ignored
No; the negative sign is essential because it identifies an inferior good
Yes; it identifies a luxury good only by magnitude
No; it identifies substitutes
legendaryBoss.feedback: Income and cross-price signs carry classification information.

legendaryBoss.q: A researcher reports cross-price elasticity of −0.9. Should the sign be discarded?
options: Yes; only magnitude matters
Yes; negative values are calculation errors
No; it indicates the goods are complements
No; it indicates both goods are inferior
legendaryBoss.feedback: The sign distinguishes complements from substitutes.

legendaryBoss.q: A government combines a tax, a binding price ceiling, and a subsidy for approved buyers in one market. What is the sound first step in elasticity analysis?
options: Add all statutory rates and assign the sum to sellers
Use demand elasticity alone for every effect
Assume the policies cancel because some raise and some lower price
Separate the policy wedges before analyzing curves, prices, and incidence
legendaryBoss.feedback: Layered policies must be decomposed before relative elasticities can be applied.

legendaryBoss.q: A firm has customer-level elasticity estimates, capacity constraints, and rising marginal cost. Why is charging the lowest price to the most elastic customers not automatically optimal?
options: Because optimal pricing must account for elasticity together with marginal cost and capacity constraints
Elasticity is irrelevant whenever capacity exists
The most elastic group should always receive the highest price
All customers must be charged marginal cost
legendaryBoss.feedback: Optimal pricing integrates demand response with costs and capacity.

legendaryBoss.q: A climate policy raises energy prices, encourages substitution, induces innovation, and changes household location over a decade. What does this imply about short-run versus long-run demand elasticity?
options: Long-run elasticity should be smaller because consumers exhaust their easiest adjustments during the first month
The relevant long-run elasticity is an equilibrium response that may exceed short-run behavioral estimates
The policy changes supply responsiveness but leaves household demand responsiveness essentially unchanged over time
The first-month estimate remains the best long-run measure because later innovation and relocation are separate effects
legendaryBoss.feedback: Technology, capital, and location adjustments expand long-run response.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says an elasticity of 0.6 is elastic because quantity changes when price changes. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Any nonzero response is elastic
Only the sign matters
Elasticity is classified by proportional magnitude; 0.6 is inelastic
Values below one are perfectly elastic
repairQuestions.feedback: A response exists, but it is proportionally smaller than the price change.

repairQuestions.q: A learner reports an elasticity in kilograms per dollar. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Elasticity is always kilograms
The units should be dollars per kilogram
Only income elasticity is unit-free
Elasticity compares percentage changes and has no measurement unit
repairQuestions.feedback: Percentage ratios cancel original units.

repairQuestions.q: A learner calls a vertical demand curve perfectly elastic. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Vertical demand is perfectly inelastic because quantity is fixed
Vertical demand is unit elastic
Vertical demand is income elastic
Vertical demand has infinite quantity response
repairQuestions.feedback: No quantity response means elasticity zero.

repairQuestions.q: A learner calls a horizontal demand curve perfectly inelastic. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Horizontal demand is unit elastic
Horizontal demand is perfectly elastic
Horizontal demand has zero response
Horizontal demand is inferior
repairQuestions.feedback: Perfectly elastic demand is horizontal.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says necessities always have perfectly inelastic demand. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Necessities are always elastic
Necessity affects supply only
Necessity matters, but so do substitutes, time, and market scope
All necessities have elasticity one
repairQuestions.feedback: Determinants are tendencies, not absolute rules.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says a steeper curve is always less elastic. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Steeper curves are always more elastic
Slope and elasticity are identical
Only curved lines have elasticity
Compare percentage responsiveness, not unit-dependent visual slope
repairQuestions.feedback: Elasticity is unit-free and location-dependent.

repairQuestions.q: A learner calculates different elasticity values for A-to-B and B-to-A. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Use midpoint averages in both percentage-change denominators
Use the first point in both directions
Average the two elasticity answers after rounding
Use only the larger endpoint
repairQuestions.feedback: The midpoint method is symmetric.

repairQuestions.q: A learner divides percentage price change by percentage quantity change for demand. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: The ratio is price change divided by income change
Divide percentage quantity change by percentage price change
Either ratio is acceptable
Use total revenue divided by price
repairQuestions.feedback: Quantity response belongs in the numerator.

repairQuestions.q: A learner reports demand elasticity as negative and classifies the good as inferior. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Negative price elasticity proves inferiority
Change the sign to identify complements
Use absolute price elasticity; income elasticity identifies inferiority
Price elasticity must be zero
repairQuestions.feedback: The demand-law sign is conventionally ignored for magnitude classification.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says a price increase always raises revenue. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Revenue always falls after a price increase
Revenue is unrelated to elasticity
Revenue rises only when supply is elastic
Revenue rises only when demand is inelastic over the relevant range
repairQuestions.feedback: The quantity response determines whether the price gain dominates.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says unit elasticity means total revenue is zero. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Unit elasticity leaves total revenue approximately unchanged
Unit elasticity means quantity is zero
Unit elasticity means price is zero
Unit elasticity means marginal cost is zero
repairQuestions.feedback: Unit elasticity marks the revenue maximum, not zero revenue.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says marginal revenue is positive on inelastic demand. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Marginal revenue is always positive
Marginal revenue is negative in the inelastic range
Marginal revenue equals price everywhere
Marginal revenue depends only on supply
repairQuestions.feedback: Expanding sales in the inelastic region reduces total revenue.

repairQuestions.q: A learner calculates supply elasticity with consumer income in the denominator. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Supply elasticity uses income change
Supply elasticity uses a rival’s price
Price elasticity of supply uses the good’s own price change
Supply elasticity equals quantity supplied
repairQuestions.feedback: Supply elasticity connects output response to output price.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says short-run supply is always more elastic. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Short-run supply is always perfectly elastic
Time affects demand only
Supply elasticity falls whenever firms enter
Longer time usually gives producers more capacity and input adjustments
repairQuestions.feedback: Adjustment options expand over time.

repairQuestions.q: A learner drops the negative sign from income elasticity. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Keep the sign because negative income elasticity identifies an inferior good
Always use absolute value for every elasticity
A negative sign indicates substitutes
The sign affects only supply elasticity
repairQuestions.feedback: Income-elasticity sign carries classification information.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says cross-price elasticity below one means goods are unrelated. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: One is the required cutoff for related goods
The sign identifies substitutes or complements; magnitude indicates strength
Only values above one are substitutes
Negative values are calculation errors
repairQuestions.feedback: Cross-price classification is based on sign, not a one-unit cutoff.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says the side that sends the tax payment to the government bears the entire tax burden. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Sellers always bear excise taxes
Buyers always bear sales taxes
Relative elasticity determines incidence, not remittance
The burden is always equal
repairQuestions.feedback: Market price adjustments distribute the burden.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says inelastic markets have no tax burden because quantity changes little. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: No quantity change means no one pays
Inelasticity eliminates price changes
Only elastic markets generate revenue
Small deadweight loss can coexist with substantial tax burden
repairQuestions.feedback: Burden and efficiency loss are different outcomes.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says the same elasticity must apply at every point on a linear demand curve. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Slope is constant, but elasticity changes with the price-to-quantity ratio
A linear curve has zero elasticity
Elasticity changes only when slope changes
All linear curves are unit elastic
repairQuestions.feedback: Point location changes percentage responsiveness.

repairQuestions.q: A learner predicts profit direction from the total-revenue test alone. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Revenue and profit are identical
Revenue direction is known; profit still requires costs
Profit depends only on elasticity
Costs affect demand rather than profit
repairQuestions.feedback: Elasticity informs revenue; cost completes profit analysis.

repairQuestions.q: After calculating a 12% increase in quantity supplied from an 8% price increase, a student reports PES = 0.67. Which step is wrong?
options: The ratio was inverted; PES = 12%/8% = 1.5
The supply response should be given a negative sign
The percentage changes should be added to get 20
The calculation should use the original price level instead
repairQuestions.feedback: Price elasticity of supply divides the percentage change in quantity supplied by the percentage change in price, so 12%/8% = 1.5.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says unused production capacity makes supply less elastic. What is the correction?
options: Unused capacity fixes quantity supplied at one level
Unused capacity affects demand elasticity but not supply
Unused capacity guarantees perfectly elastic supply
Unused capacity usually makes it easier to expand output, increasing supply elasticity
repairQuestions.feedback: Spare capacity lets firms respond to higher prices without first building entirely new capacity.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says input mobility has no effect on supply elasticity. Best repair?
options: Only demand-side substitutes affect elasticity
Input mobility changes the sign of supply elasticity
Inputs that can be reallocated easily generally make supply more elastic
Input mobility makes supply perfectly inelastic
repairQuestions.feedback: Flexible inputs let producers change output more readily when price changes.

repairQuestions.q: A learner gets PES = 0.4 and calls supply elastic. What should be corrected?
options: The sign alone determines elastic versus inelastic
A coefficient below one is inelastic over the measured range
Any positive coefficient is elastic
A coefficient below one is perfectly elastic
repairQuestions.feedback: For PES, magnitude below one means quantity supplied responds proportionally less than price.

repairQuestions.q: A learner sees income elasticity of -0.5 and labels the good a necessity. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: The negative sign identifies an inferior good for the measured consumers
Any coefficient below one identifies a normal necessity
Negative income elasticity means the goods are complements
The coefficient measures price responsiveness, not income responsiveness
repairQuestions.feedback: Negative income elasticity means demand falls when income rises.

repairQuestions.q: Income rises 10% and quantity demanded rises 5%. A learner reports income elasticity of 2. What went wrong?
options: The sign should be negative because income rose
The correct value is 15 because percentages are added
Income elasticity cannot be calculated from percentage changes
The ratio was reversed; the elasticity is 0.5
repairQuestions.feedback: Income elasticity is %ΔQd divided by %Δincome, so 5%/10% = 0.5.

repairQuestions.q: A learner sees cross-price elasticity of +0.9 and says the goods are complements. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: A positive coefficient indicates complements
The sign identifies normal versus inferior goods
Cross-price elasticity cannot classify related goods
A positive coefficient indicates substitutes
repairQuestions.feedback: Demand for one good moves with the other good’s price when the goods are substitutes.

repairQuestions.q: The price of good Y rises 8% and demand for good X rises 4%. A learner reports cross-price elasticity of 2. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: The ratio is 12 because the percentages are added
Cross-price elasticity uses X’s own price change
The ratio is 4%/8% = 0.5
The ratio must be negative because price rose
repairQuestions.feedback: Cross-price elasticity divides the percentage change in demand for X by the percentage change in the price of Y.

repairQuestions.q: A learner calculates total revenue by adding price and quantity. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Divide price by quantity
Add consumer and producer surplus
Multiply price by quantity sold
Subtract quantity from price
repairQuestions.feedback: Total revenue is P × Q.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says a price cut always lowers total revenue because each unit sells for less. What is missing?
options: A price cut always makes demand inelastic
Quantity may rise enough to increase revenue when demand is elastic
Quantity demanded never changes with price
Revenue depends only on fixed cost
repairQuestions.feedback: The total-revenue test compares the price change with the percentage quantity response.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says marginal revenue must be positive everywhere on a downward-sloping demand curve. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Marginal revenue becomes zero near unit elasticity and negative on the inelastic portion
Marginal revenue is always equal to price
Marginal revenue is negative only when demand is perfectly elastic
Elasticity has no relationship to marginal revenue
repairQuestions.feedback: For a standard downward-sloping demand curve, MR is positive on the elastic portion, zero near unit elasticity, and negative on the inelastic portion.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says a price-based policy will reduce quantity by the same percentage in every market. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Elasticity affects revenue but not policy responses
Quantity response depends on the relevant elasticity
Every market has unit-elastic demand
Only supply shifts can change quantity
repairQuestions.feedback: More elastic buyers or sellers respond more strongly to price incentives.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says labor demand elasticity is unrelated to substitution possibilities. Best correction?
options: More available substitutes for a type of labor generally make labor demand more elastic
Substitutes make labor demand perfectly inelastic
Factor demand elasticity depends only on worker preferences
Substitution changes labor supply but never labor demand
repairQuestions.feedback: Employers can respond more strongly to wage changes when alternative inputs are available.

repairQuestions.q: A learner says supply elasticity does not matter when the price received for an export rises. Which statement best corrects the error?
options: Export prices affect demand only
Supply elasticity matters only in closed markets
More elastic supply means output cannot change
More elastic supply allows a larger output response to the higher price
repairQuestions.feedback: Trade price changes generate larger production responses when supply is more elastic.

bridgeQuestions.q: Demand for a product is less elastic than supply. Which concept uses this difference in elasticity to determine who bears more of a tax?
options: Comparative advantage
GDP measurement
Economic tax incidence
Money creation
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Relative elasticity determines economic tax incidence.

bridgeQuestions.q: A tax creates a larger quantity reduction in a highly elastic market. Which concept measures the resulting lost gains from trade?
options: Income inequality only
Nominal GDP
Money neutrality
Deadweight loss
bridgeQuestions.feedback: The lost trades create deadweight loss.

bridgeQuestions.q: A monopolist faces less elastic demand. Which market-structure result is most consistent with that condition?
options: The firm can sustain a larger markup
The market becomes perfectly competitive
Marginal cost becomes zero
Consumer surplus must rise
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Market power is stronger when buyers have fewer substitutes.

bridgeQuestions.q: Consumer surplus changes after a price increase. Which elasticity fact predicts whether quantity contracts a little or a lot?
options: Price elasticity of supply only
Price elasticity of demand
Income elasticity of supply
The GDP deflator
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Demand elasticity governs the quantity response that shapes surplus loss.

bridgeQuestions.q: A tariff raises the domestic price of an import. Which elasticity predicts the size of the import decline?
options: Income elasticity of domestic supply
Price elasticity of money demand
Elasticity of import demand
Labor-supply elasticity only
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Import-demand responsiveness drives the quantity effect.

bridgeQuestions.q: A wage increase changes employment. Which area of microeconomics applies elasticity to the demand for inputs such as labor?
options: Public goods
Consumer choice only
Perfect competition in money markets
Factor markets
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Labor demand is a derived factor demand.

bridgeQuestions.q: An emissions tax changes output. Which concept explains why a corrective tax may be justified in the first place?
options: Externalities
Monetary neutrality
Income effects only
Comparative advantage
bridgeQuestions.feedback: The external cost motivates correction; elasticity predicts response.

bridgeQuestions.q: A binding rent ceiling creates a shortage. Which elasticity determines how strongly quantity supplied shrinks over time?
options: Income elasticity of demand
Price elasticity of supply
Cross-price elasticity only
Elasticity of money supply
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Long-run housing supply elasticity drives the supply response.

bridgeQuestions.q: A minimum price raises quantity supplied. Which elasticity predicts the surplus expansion from the supply side?
options: Price elasticity of demand only
Income elasticity
Price elasticity of supply
Cross-price elasticity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Supply elasticity predicts output expansion.

bridgeQuestions.q: A perfectly competitive firm faces horizontal demand at the market price. Which elasticity description fits firm-level demand?
options: Perfectly inelastic
Unit elastic
Negative income elastic
Perfectly elastic
bridgeQuestions.feedback: A price-taking firm can sell at the market price but not above it.

bridgeQuestions.q: Differentiation in monopolistic competition gives a firm fewer close substitutes than perfect competition. What is the elasticity implication?
options: Firm demand becomes less elastic
Firm demand becomes perfectly elastic
Supply becomes vertical
Income elasticity becomes negative
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Differentiation reduces immediate substitution.

bridgeQuestions.q: Strategic rivals in an oligopoly may match a price cut. Why does this complicate a firm’s elasticity estimate?
options: Elasticity applies only to monopoly
Rival reactions and substitution jointly shape the response
Rival reactions make demand vertical
Price changes no longer affect quantity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Strategic response changes the residual demand facing the firm.

bridgeQuestions.q: A budget line rotates after a price change. Which elasticity summarizes the resulting proportional quantity response for one good?
options: Price elasticity of supply
Cross-price elasticity of firms
Price elasticity of demand
Tax elasticity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Consumer choice generates the demand response summarized by elasticity.

bridgeQuestions.q: Competition introduces more close substitutes. Which elasticity effect supports competitive-market discipline?
options: Demand facing each seller becomes more inelastic
Market supply becomes perfectly fixed
Income elasticity becomes zero
Demand facing each seller becomes more elastic
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Switching among sellers limits price increases.

bridgeQuestions.q: A price change creates both substitution and income effects. Which measure summarizes their combined percentage quantity response?
options: Price elasticity of demand
Price elasticity of supply
Tax incidence
Producer surplus
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Observed demand elasticity reflects the total quantity response.

bridgeQuestions.q: A firm’s marginal cost rises. Which elasticity helps predict how much the firm can pass through in price?
options: Income elasticity alone
Elasticity of demand facing the firm
Supply elasticity of consumers
GDP elasticity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Less elastic customer demand supports greater pass-through.

bridgeQuestions.q: A public good is financed through taxation. Which elasticities help determine how strongly the tax distorts the market being taxed?
options: The public good’s nonrivalry alone
Income elasticity of government
Demand and supply elasticities in the tax base
Cross-price elasticity of money
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Tax-base responsiveness determines the lost transactions.

bridgeQuestions.q: Better consumer information lowers search costs. Which elasticity change is most likely in differentiated markets?
options: Demand becomes perfectly inelastic
Supply becomes vertical
Income elasticity must turn negative
Demand becomes more elastic as comparison improves
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Information can strengthen substitution and competition.

bridgeQuestions.q: A behavioral bias makes consumers slow to switch after a price increase. How does standard elasticity analysis record the observed effect?
options: As lower short-run demand elasticity
As higher supply elasticity
As negative cross-price elasticity automatically
As zero scarcity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Inertia reduces the measured short-run quantity response.

bridgeQuestions.q: Comparative advantage predicts gains from specialization. Which elasticity determines how strongly trade quantities react to changes in relative prices?
options: Income elasticity only
Trade-related demand and supply elasticities
Perfectly inelastic domestic demand by assumption
No elasticity is relevant to trade volumes
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Comparative advantage explains gains; elasticity shapes the size of quantity adjustments.

bridgeQuestions.q: A commodity price rises 10% and quantity supplied rises 15%. What does this imply about the responsiveness of producers?
options: Producers show an elastic supply response
Producers show an inelastic supply response
Quantity supplied did not respond
The result measures demand, not supply
bridgeQuestions.feedback: A 15% quantity response to a 10% price change gives PES above one.

bridgeQuestions.q: Why does a longer time horizon often connect supply elasticity to investment decisions?
options: Longer horizons make all prices fixed
Firms lose the ability to change inputs over time
Supply becomes unrelated to marginal cost
Firms have more time to add capacity and reorganize production
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Investment and capacity adjustment make long-run supply more responsive.

bridgeQuestions.q: How does inventory management connect to supply elasticity?
options: Inventory affects only consumer demand
Stored goods make supply vertical by definition
Stored inventory can be released when price rises, increasing quantity responsiveness
Inventory prevents firms from reacting to price
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Storage creates another margin through which sellers can respond to price changes.

bridgeQuestions.q: A market has highly mobile labor and equipment. What does that suggest about the supply response to a price increase?
options: The price increase cannot affect production
Output can adjust more strongly because inputs can move toward the market
Output must remain fixed because mobile inputs leave the market
Demand becomes more elastic while supply is unchanged
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Input mobility links production flexibility to greater supply elasticity.

bridgeQuestions.q: A grocery chain expects household incomes to rise. Which use of income elasticity is most direct?
options: Calculate the money multiplier
Find the slope of the supply curve
Forecast which product categories may gain or lose demand
Determine the legal incidence of a sales tax
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Income elasticity helps firms anticipate demand shifts as consumer income changes.

bridgeQuestions.q: A category has income elasticity 1.4. How does that connect to business forecasting during an expansion?
options: The category must be a complement to every other good
Demand may grow more than proportionally with income
Demand must fall as income rises
Quantity supplied must fall by 1.4%
bridgeQuestions.feedback: An elasticity above one indicates a strong positive demand response to income growth.

bridgeQuestions.q: Why can income elasticity help explain changes in the mix of goods consumers buy as an economy grows?
options: Normal, luxury, and inferior goods respond differently to rising income
All goods have identical income responses
Income elasticity measures only producer costs
It fixes consumer preferences at one bundle
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Different income responses shift the composition of demand as purchasing power changes.

bridgeQuestions.q: A coffee shop tracks the price of a nearby competitor’s drinks. Why is cross-price elasticity useful?
options: It determines the legal tax rate
It indicates how the competitor’s price may shift demand for the shop’s drinks
It measures the shop’s fixed cost
It identifies the money supply
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Cross-price elasticity connects substitute pricing to demand shifts.

bridgeQuestions.q: A console maker lowers console prices. Why might a game publisher care about cross-price elasticity?
options: Negative cross-price elasticity would imply game demand rises as console price falls
Positive income elasticity guarantees game demand falls
Supply elasticity determines whether consoles and games are complements
Cross-price elasticity is unrelated to complementary products
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Complementary goods connect through opposite movements between one price and the other good’s demand.

bridgeQuestions.q: Two brands have cross-price elasticity near +2. What strategic connection does that suggest?
options: They are strong complements
They are unrelated goods
They must have identical marginal costs
Their demand is strongly linked as substitutes
bridgeQuestions.feedback: A large positive cross-price coefficient signals a strong substitution relationship.

bridgeQuestions.q: How does the total-revenue formula connect a demand curve to firm revenue?
options: The demand slope directly equals total revenue
Revenue is the area above demand and below price
Quantity alone determines revenue
Each price-quantity point implies revenue equal to P × Q
bridgeQuestions.feedback: A point on demand supplies the price and quantity needed to calculate revenue.

bridgeQuestions.q: A firm cuts price and total revenue rises. What does this imply about demand over that price range?
options: Quantity demanded must have fallen
Price and quantity effects always cancel
Customers were responsive enough for the quantity gain to dominate
Demand was perfectly inelastic
bridgeQuestions.feedback: The total-revenue test translates elasticity into a practical pricing signal.

bridgeQuestions.q: Why is unit elasticity a useful benchmark for revenue management on a linear demand curve?
options: It makes demand perfectly horizontal
It is near the point where total revenue is maximized
It guarantees profit is maximized regardless of cost
It makes marginal cost zero
bridgeQuestions.feedback: At unit elasticity the price and quantity percentage effects offset, marking the revenue peak on a standard linear demand curve.

bridgeQuestions.q: How does elasticity connect to marginal-revenue reasoning for a firm with downward-sloping demand?
options: MR is positive on the elastic portion and negative on the inelastic portion
MR is always zero when price changes
Elasticity determines fixed cost rather than MR
MR is positive only when demand is perfectly inelastic
bridgeQuestions.feedback: The elasticity region helps identify the sign of marginal revenue.

bridgeQuestions.q: A tax raises the price buyers pay. Why can demand elasticity matter for the seller’s revenue response?
options: It fixes the statutory tax rate
It determines the seller’s fixed cost
It guarantees producer surplus rises
It determines how strongly quantity demanded falls as the buyer price rises
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Revenue consequences depend on the quantity response to the effective price change.

bridgeQuestions.q: A seller receives $18 per unit and sells 400 units after a market change. Which measure combines these two values when evaluating the revenue effect?
options: Producer surplus always equals total revenue
Cross-price elasticity equals $18 × 400
Total revenue equals the price received times quantity sold
Consumer surplus equals price times quantity
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Elasticity analysis often evaluates how price and quantity changes combine to change revenue.
